pr_title: Allow wildcards at the end of index names for API Keys and Tenant tokens
pr_body:
This PR introduces the wildcards at the end of the index names when identifying indexes in the API Keys and tenant tokens. It fixes #2788 and fixes #2908. This PR is based on @akhildevelops' work.

Note that when a tenant token filter is chosen to restrict a search, it is always the most restrictive pattern that is chosen. If we have an index pattern _prod*_ that defines _filter1_ and _p*_ that defines _filter2_, the engine will choose _filter1_ over _filter2_ as it is defined for a most restrictive pattern, _prod*_. This restrictiveness is defined by 1. is it exact, without _*_ 2. the length of the pattern.

It is a continuation of work that has already started and should close #2869.

issue_context.title: Use wildcard (`*`) at the end of the index names when creating API keys
issue_context.body:
Following
- this product discussion: https://github.com/meilisearch/product/discussions/491
- this spec: https://github.com/meilisearch/specifications/pull/189

## Goal

Allow using the wildcard `*` at the end of the index name (in `indexes` field) when creating API keys

## How does it work?

When [creating an API key](https://docs.meilisearch.com/reference/api/keys.html#create-a-key), the `*` should be available this ways:

```bash
curl \
  -X POST 'http://localhost:7700/keys' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer MASTER_KEY' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data-binary '{
    "description": "Add documents: Products API key",
    "actions": ["documents.add"],
    "indexes": ["products_*"],
    "expiresAt": "2042-04-02T00:42:42Z"
  }'
```

This means the newly created keys will be available for the `products_main`, `products_dev`, but not for `products`

#### Additional explanation of the matching

The `books*` expression will match the following indexes: `books`, `books_staging`, but NOT `book` (without `s`)

#### Errors

- if no indexes are matched, no error are thrown during the API key creation. However this key will be useless until a matching index is created

## Impacted teams

Pinging @meilisearch/docs-team, but also @meilisearch/integration-team (I'm not sure for you)

--- 

## Todo
- [ ] Implementation the changes -> Open to external contributions
- [X] Update the spec -> https://github.com/meilisearch/specifications/pull/189


---
Feel free to ask any questions to implement this issue. The core team is available to guide you through this contribution, even if it's your first one.
We recommend referring to the [CONTRIBUTING.md guidelines](https://github.com/meilisearch/meilisearch/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md), especially if it's your first contribution to this repository.
Thanks in advance for your involvement ❤️

- Can the wildcard be at the start of the pattern? `*_end`
- Can it be in the middle of the pattern? `start_*_end`
- Can there be multiple wildcards in a single pattern? `start_*_middle_*_end`
- Can it be at the start and the end? `*_middle_*`

Cases that don't make much sense:
- Can a wildcard follow a wildcard? `start_**_end`
- Can a key index be all wildcards? `****`

From what I understand of the product discussion, what we want here is;
> It could make the creation of an API key easier and faster in case several indexes are **prefixed** by a fixed string and need to be accessible by the same key.

This means we only accept API keys that end with a wildcard and nothing more.
Thus only `start_*` and none of your examples.

Just to be absolutely sure, can you confirm @gmourier?
I've started working on this feature. Will give a PR shortly.

@Ugzuzg Do you have particular needs for these syntaxes?
Not really. I wanted to start working on this, so tried to clear up the requirements.

> What's the idea behind using (uid, action, index_name) as key for action_keyid_index_expiration database ?
> 
> Can just use (UID,) as the key old_key.

I've got it, keys are hashed with respect to uid ,index_name, and action. For every request, uid, index_name and action are extracted and then compared with the hashed keys of action_keyid_index_expiration database.

For implementing the index pattern, I think we need to take out the index_name from the key and put into value as series of indexes. i.e, `uid, action` will be key  and `all indexes, key_expires at` form the values.

Thanks, @irevoire and @Ugzuzg!

In my opinion, these patterns can be adapted to most cases. Others can be added if needed and expressed.

- `*_end`
- `start_*_end`
- `start_*`

🤓 I think It should also be integrated into the `searchRules` of the tenant tokens.

Discussed with the team: this issue is finally not about "globing" but only allowing the `*` character at the END of the `indexes` field when creating API key. I've clarify the issue accordingly.

The other patterns described in this issue are still relevant but lead to
- more product discussion: it means creating a real globing, and so, which globbing RFC do we want to follow? Bash? Another?
- how do we want to implement this regarding the code base?

📣 If anyone here thinks the globing can be relevant in their use case or have ideas about implementation, let us know about your use case and what you would expect to have as feature here: https://github.com/meilisearch/product/discussions/491. It will be really helpful for us, so thanks in advance 🙏
